equity_bridge.note: $446m surplus at 2025-12-31 after the December 2025 group-annuity settlement ($13m cash, $243m short-term bond fund, $190m GPC stock; GPC_Annual_FY2025.txt:2493), earmarked to fund US defined-contribution (Qualified Replacement Plan) contributions from 2027 that would otherwise be cash opex inside EBITDA. Added at ~76% (24% tax) because the funding displaces deductible cash contributions. Forward flows carry no pension income, so the matching-asset rule is satisfied. Vintage: 2025-12-31; the $190m GPC-stock component moves with the share price.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case organic growth (comparable sales + price). Equity 5yr CAGR of 6.6% and revenue 5yr CAGR of 8.0% both include 2-3pp/yr of acquired growth (FY2022 included the $1.3bn KDG deal) funded by acquisition spend that is outside FCF; the FCF build charges capex only, so the matching growth rate is organic. Comps: FY2024 -0.8%, FY2025 +0.9%, 9M 2026 ~+2.9%.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020 $16,537m -> FY2025 $24,300m (5yr 8.0%); FY2022 $22,096m -> FY2025 (3yr 3.2%). EPS CAGRs use ADJUSTED diluted EPS ($5.27 FY2020, $8.31 FY2022, $7.37 FY2025) because GAAP FY2025 EPS of $0.47 is distorted by the pension settlement, First Brands and asbestos charges. Equity FY2020 $3,218m -> FY2025 $4,440m. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC and equity-award taxes): FY2022 ~$1,072m -> FY2025 $355.5m, a -30.8%/yr print driven by the FY2025 working-capital trough, not a trend; the 5yr figure is null because FY2020 OCF is not in the metrics table. SBC is not growing faster than cash flow in any structural sense (0.2-0.3% of revenue throughout); the owner-FCF/reported-FCF gap is small and stable.

scenario_narratives.base: A mature, moderately cyclical distributor returning to its FY2024-25 earnings power after a two-year restructuring and separation cost cycle. Organic growth of ~3% (price/mix plus a little volume from the old US car parc and a normalising industrial cycle), no acquisition contribution, and a pre-SBC EBITDA margin that rebuilds from 7.3% (FY2026, after ~$250m of restructuring and separation cash) to 8.6% by FY2030 -- back to, not beyond, the FY2024 level. Owner FCF recovers from the FY2025 working-capital trough ($355m) toward ~$1.3bn by year 5 as the one-offs roll off. Terminal value bound by the 15x cap. The separation is neutral in this case: focus benefits offset stranded costs.
scenario_narratives.bull: The aftermarket's 5% industry growth and a Motion upcycle lift organic growth to 4-4.5%; pricing and sourcing initiatives (gross margin +50-70bp a year in 2025-26) finally outrun opex inflation once restructuring is complete, taking the margin to 9.5% pre-SBC. Two focused companies after Q1 2027 allocate capital better and the market re-rates the industrial half toward peer multiples -- captured here through flows and a 3.0% terminal rate, not a higher exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Thin North America Automotive margins (~7%) offer no cushion against persistent wage, healthcare, rent and Middle East-driven freight inflation; guidance has already been cut once in 2026. Growth stalls at ~1% for two years on weak Europe and a soft US PMI. The separation adds leverage (new $1bn Term Loan A, debt ~$5.1bn, 2.0x+ EBITDA, negative rating outlooks), management distraction under a new CEO, and permanent stranded costs. Another adverse asbestos remeasurement or supplier failure like First Brands recurs.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value GPC as what it is today -- one consolidated distributor earning ~8.3% adjusted EBITDA margins on $24-26bn of sales -- on an owner-FCF basis that charges SBC, restructuring and separation cash as real costs and gives no credit for acquisitions it has not yet paid for. The FY2025 GAAP collapse is noise (pension settlement, First Brands, asbestos); the FY2025 FCF trough is mostly working capital; neither is the run-rate, so the forward build is from components anchored on adjusted EBITDA and FY2021-24 cash conversion. The pending Global Automotive / Global Industrial separation is not modelled as a sum-of-the-parts because no standalone financials exist yet; it is carried in the scenario spread (focus upside in the bull, stranded costs and leverage in the bear) and in a 25% bear weight. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF, which the stock's own adjusted P/E history supports, and the cap binds in every scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Separation execution: delay, higher one-off costs, permanent dis-synergies/stranded costs, two smaller and more levered balance sheets; also two new boards and a CEO transition in the same window
Margin fragility: North America Automotive EBITDA margin ~7%; wage, healthcare, rent and freight/fuel inflation (Middle East conflict) have already forced a 2026 guidance cut
Leverage: total debt ~$5.1bn at Q3 2026 (2.0x+ adjusted EBITDA), $1bn Term Loan A maturing Oct 2027, negative rating outlooks; refinancing through the separation
Cyclicality of the Industrial segment (37% of sales) to US manufacturing PMI, and weak European consumer demand in International Automotive
Supplier concentration and credit: First Brands' bankruptcy cost $151m; ~55% of US automotive inventory comes from 10 suppliers
Asbestos: $317m discounted liability with actuarial remeasurement risk ($103m adverse in FY2025)
Working-capital volatility: FY2025 FCF was half of trend; 9M 2026 OCF included a non-recurring $250m A/R sale benefit

Acquisition dependence: historical growth was 2-3pp/yr acquired; the base case gives no credit for future M&A, but if management keeps buying at FY2024 prices with debt the organic FCF here is overstated

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 90.78-151.57
data_sources.financials: GPC_Annual_FY2025.txt (10-K, FY ended 2025-12-31) for adjusted EBITDA, SBC, equity-award withholding, pension surplus, asbestos liability, cash taxes; GPC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (10-Q, 2026-09-30) for cash, debt, lease liabilities, diluted shares, 9M 2026 results and separation disclosures; GPC_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized for the FY2016-FY2025 history and segment KPIs
data_sources.qualitative: GPC_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): segment mix, competitive position, separation timeline, FY2026 guidance as of the 2026-10-20 Q3 release, bull/bear axes

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average common shares assuming dilution, Q3 2026 (138,331k; GPC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1300). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. GPC repurchased no stock in FY2025 or 9M 2026, so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding with buybacks.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back $48,847k (GPC_Annual_FY2025.txt:2567) PLUS net-share-settlement withholding of $16,671k recorded as 'Shares issued from employee incentive plans' in financing (GPC_Annual_FY2025.txt:2587). GPC publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back SBC, so ebitda_margin_path is stated pre-SBC.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:03Z regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~9.3% (10y UST ~4.3%, ERP 5%, beta ~1.0 for a BBB-/Baa1 distributor with negative outlook at S&P/Moody's). Pre-tax cost of debt 4.09% (Q3 2026 10-Q average cost of debt), 3.1% after 24% tax. Market cap ~$17.0bn vs $4.7bn debt gives ~78/22 weights -> 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality, separation and leverage risk are charged in the flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease expense is inside SG&A and lease cash is inside operating cash flow, so the full lease cost is already charged within the EBITDA margin path. Operating lease liabilities ($1,713.9m at 2026-09-30, GPC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1020) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. No separate lease_cost_pct_path (would double-charge). Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests $17.4m at FY2025 (GPC_Annual_FY2025.txt:2467); 10-K states NCI net income is not material. Ignored; no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (routing table row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md; US filer so the currency sections do not apply, lease and charge-risk-once sections do). GPC is a value-added distributor (NAPA/UAP, AAG, Repco, Motion Industries) whose value is a stream of free cash flow; not a bank/REIT/LIC. BASE YEAR: FY2025 GAAP net income of $66m (-92.7%) is distorted by a $742m US pension settlement charge (largely non-cash reclassification from AOCI), a $151m First Brands bankruptcy credit loss and a $103m asbestos liability remeasurement; the anchor is instead adjusted EBITDA $2,005.6m (8.3% margin, flat on FY2024), stated pre-SBC at 8.45% (GPC_Annual_FY2025.txt:2140). FY2025 reported FCF ($421m) was also depressed by working capital (unwind of 2024 deferred-payment inventory purchases, First Brands non-payment, tax-planning payments); FY2021-24 reported FCF averaged ~$930m, so last_fcf of $355.5m is a trough, not the run-rate, and the forward build is from components. RESTRUCTURING/SEPARATION: 'adjusted' figures exclude ~$200m/yr of restructuring cash since 2024 and $55m of separation costs through 9M 2026; these are real cash and are charged inside the margin path in FY2026-FY2027 (year-1 pre-SBC margin 7.3% vs 8.45% underlying), tapering to zero by FY2029. ACQUISITIONS: 2-3pp/yr of historical sales growth was acquired (KPI AcquisitionSalesGrowthContribution) with $300m-$1.1bn/yr of acquisition spend that sits outside FCF; the growth path is therefore ORGANIC ONLY (comps + price), so revenue and capex are on the same footing. INTEREST INCOME: company is net-debt (~2.0x adjusted EBITDA), nothing stripped. ASBESTOS: $317m discounted liability; ongoing claim payments are expensed within Corporate EBITDA and thus inside the flows, so it is not added to net debt (doing both would double-charge); the remeasurement risk is a bear-case item. FY2026 GUIDANCE (Q3 2026, 2026-10-20): adjusted diluted EPS narrowed to $7.50-$7.75 on $30-40m of Middle East conflict freight/fuel costs; 9M 2026 sales +5.6%, adjusted EBITDA margin 8.3%, comps positive in all three segments. A $250m A/R Sales Agreement benefit flatters 9M 2026 OCF and is not treated as recurring. SEPARATION: the Global Automotive / Global Industrial split (announced 2026-02-17, targeted Q1 2027) is valued here as the consolidated entity on combined flows because no standalone financials exist yet; it is handled as a bull-case re-rating/focus upside and a bear-case dis-synergy, stranded-cost and leverage risk, not as a deal-completes/deal-breaks model, since the business continues either way.

bear.narrative: FY2026 finishes at the low end of guidance; FY2027-28 organic growth stalls near 1% as European consumers stay weak, US industrial PMI rolls over and fuel/freight inflation persists. The separation runs over cost and time, leaves ~0.5pp of permanent stranded and dis-synergy costs, and the margin never recovers past 7.6% pre-SBC; asbestos claims trend adverse again. Same WACC; terminal growth 2.0%.

base.growth_note: FY2026 5.5% is the 9M 2026 actual run-rate (+5.6%, incl. ~1pp acquisitions and ~2pp FX that have already happened). From FY2027 organic only: ~2-3% price/mix plus modest volume from a record-old US car parc and a recovering industrial PMI; no acquisition contribution (see inputs.notes). Decelerates to the 2.5% terminal rate.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC. Underlying FY2025 adjusted margin 8.3% (8.45% pre-SBC); FY2024 8.5%. FY2026 7.3% = ~8.55% underlying (9M 2026 8.34% adjusted + SBC) less ~1.3pp of restructuring ($193m 9M) and separation ($55m 9M) cash costs. FY2027 7.8% carries the separation-completion year costs and early stranded/dis-synergy costs. Matures at 8.6% pre-SBC (~8.35% on GPC's adjusted definition) -- i.e. a return to the FY2024-25 level, not expansion; gross-margin gains from pricing/sourcing are assumed to be absorbed by wage, healthcare, rent and freight inflation, as they were in 2025.
base.sbc_note: FY2025 SBC incl. withholding $65.5m / $24,300m = 0.27%; 9M 2026 ($45.1m + $13.7m) / $19,323m = 0.30%. Held flat; GPC is a low-SBC issuer and there is no evidence of a glide in either direction.
base.da_note: FY2025 D&A $538m includes a $42m one-off depreciation adjustment; ex that $496m = 2.0%. 9M 2026 $403m annualises to ~2.1% on technology and supply-chain investment. Includes ~$150m+/yr of acquired-intangible amortisation.
base.capex_note: FY2023 2.2%, FY2024 2.4%, FY2025 1.9%, 9M 2026 1.6% ($314m). 2.0% is the three-year average; D&A modestly exceeds capex because acquired-intangible amortisation has no capex counterpart.
base.cash_tax_note: FY2024 GAAP effective rate 23.1% ($271.9m on $1,176m pre-tax); GPC's adjusted tax rate ~24%. FY2025 cash taxes of $221m were low because of the one-off charges and are not a run-rate. US 21% federal plus state, plus higher-rate European and Australasian jurisdictions.
base.wc_note: Negative: a distributor with inventory ($5bn+) and receivables carries more operating capital than its payables, even with GPC's supplier-financing programmes. Each $1 of revenue growth consumes ~$0.08 of cash. FY2024-25 working-capital outflows were larger than this because of the deferred-payment inventory unwind and First Brands; -8% is the steady-state assumption.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0%/2.5% implies 18.6x terminal FCF; the 15x cap binds, per the method's 12-15x guidance for cyclical/slow-growth businesses. 15x owner FCF is consistent with the stock's own 15-17x adjusted P/E range.

bull.narrative: Organic growth 4-4.5% through FY2029 as the US aftermarket grows ~5% on a 12.8-year car parc and Motion rides an industrial upcycle; separation lands on time in Q1 2027 with restructuring savings and gross-margin initiatives finally flowing through to a 9.5% pre-SBC margin (~9.3% adjusted, roughly the FY2022-23 peak). Same WACC and cap; terminal growth 3.0%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because leverage has risen into the separation (debt $4.3bn -> $5.1bn in nine months, negative outlooks at S&P and Moody's), FY2026 guidance has already been narrowed downward once, and the FY2025 print showed how quickly one-offs (supplier failure, asbestos, pension) hit a 7-8% margin business. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: an industrial upcycle, margin expansion that has eluded GPC for three years, and a clean, on-time separation under a new CEO. Base at 50%: the business is mature and predictable at the sales line; the uncertainty is in margin and execution, which the tails carry.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
